data.title: Nasdaq futures jump on hopes for strong Anthropic market debut
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Nasdaq futures rose nearly 2% on Thursday after Anthropic priced its IPO above the marketed range, bolstering expectations for a strong debut and reviving sentiment around beaten-down AI stocks.

Anthropic priced its upsized offering at $83 per share, above its $70 to $78 range, raising $81 billion in the largest listing on record that valued the AI lab at about $1.5 trillion. It will begin trading on the Nasdaq later in the day.

The listing follows weeks of selling in chipmakers and cloud companies, as investors fretted over stretched valuations, hefty spending on AI infrastructure and the sudden exit of Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang, a pillar of the industry's growth.

Nvidia shares rose 1.6% in premarket trading. The chipmaker had fallen for five straight sessions through Wednesday, as upbeat revenue forecast did little to uplift sentiment.

Among other chipmakers, Intel, Advanced Micro Devices, Micron, and Marvell rose between 3% and 4.5%.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius gained 3.5% and 4.6%, respectively, while data center-related companies IREN and Applied Digital climbed 4.5% each.

At 04:13 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 301 points, or 0.6%, S&P 500 E-minis were up 76 points, or 1.04%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 494.25 points, or 1.83%.

The S&P 500 logged its fifth consecutive session of decline on Wednesday, with Hawkish minutes from the US Federal Reserve's latest meeting also weighing on sentiment.

Nearly all Fed officials saw a need for more rate increases if the economy performed as projected, while a few warned that inflation could be stickier than anticipated and could call for tighter policy.

Traders are pricing in near-certainty of a 25-basis-point hike at the Fed's December meeting and about an 8% chance of a 50-basis-point move, according to LSEG data.

Walmart is scheduled to report quarterly earnings before the opening bell on Thursday.

Take-Two Interactive shares were up 0.9%, after sharp gains in previous session, following the global launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI."

(Reporting by Medha Singh and Utkarsh Hathi in Bengaluru; Editing by Ronojoy Mazumdar and Shilpi Majumdar)

data.title: Almost All Fed Officials See Need For Additional Rate Hikes, October Minutes Show
data.description:
03:29 PM EST, 11/18/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Almost all Federal Reserve officials agreed that interest rates must rise further to cool inflation, minutes from the central bank's October meeting showed Wednesday.

In a split vote on Oct. 28, the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee held its policy rate steady after a 25-basis-point hike in September. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack preferred another quarter-percentage-point hike last month.

"Almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate -- broadly consistent with the September Summary of Economic Projections -- would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2% objective," the minutes showed.

A couple of participants at the October meeting said the Fed may need to raise its policy rate by more than 25 basis points at the next meeting if incoming inflation data were unfavorable, according to the minutes.

US inflation has remained above the Fed's 2% target for nearly six years. Most participants at the October FOMC meeting viewed price pressures to be broad based and expected inflation to remain elevated in the near term, the minutes showed.

"Many participants viewed the (artificial intelligence) buildout as a material source of inflation risk," according to the minutes.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC Wednesday that the central bank may need to lift interest rates aggressively because inflation was "headed in the wrong direction."

The minutes showed a "stronger conviction in further hikes than (Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's post-meeting) press conference conveyed, with disagreement mainly over timing, a message we have received from Fed speakers since this meeting," said Vikram Rai, senior economist at TD Economics.

Fed Governor Michael Barr said Wednesday that raising interest rates will be appropriate to bring inflation down to the 2% target in a timely manner, joining other central bank officials who have recently leaned hawkish.

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said on Tuesday that the FOMC will likely need to lift its policy rate "several" times before spring. Hammack has also pushed for policy tightening, though she recently said that it must be undertaken gradually.

Markets widely expect the central bank to raise its benchmark lending rate by 25 basis points next month, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

"A 25-basis-point December increase looks consistent with the broad consensus, but it is not assured, and a larger move is a conditional minority view," TD Economics' Rai said. "Broader inflation pass-through could require more restriction, while weaker AI investment and improving supply could limit it."

data.title: OBSBOT Tail Air 2 Advances Professional Video Production with 1-Inch 4K Imaging, OBSBOT Log and Greater Flexibility
data.description:
Shenzhen, China, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- OBSBOT, an industry leader in smart videography technology, today officially unveiled OBSBOT Tail Air 2, an AI-powered PTZR camera designed for flexible video production. Combining a 1-inch CMOS sensor, 4K/60 imaging, OBSBOT Log, and Custom 3D LUTs, Tail Air 2 delivers professional-quality imaging with greater control over color and detail. AI Tracking 2.0, upgraded AI Director Grids, and automated camera movements reduce manual operation, while motorized PTZR, uncropped vertical 4K/60 recording, and native IP connectivity allow creators to adapt to different shooting setups, content formats, and multi-camera workflows.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/5d77c836-351f-490d-986a-f14f1feca6b1/obsbot-tail-air1.png

“Creators shouldn't have to choose between image quality, creative control, and production efficiency,” said Liu Bo, CEO of OBSBOT. “With Tail Air 2, we're bringing these capabilities together, making professional-quality video production simpler and giving creators more freedom to focus on their content.”

A 1-Inch Sensor That Brings More to Every Frame

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/6d5ff73d-b463-41f9-8db1-b389401aae98/obsbot-tail-air2.png

Tail Air 2 features a 1-inch CMOS sensor with 3.2 μm pixels, an f/1.9 aperture, and an eight-element optical lens. It captures detailed 4K footage at up to 60fps and 1080p video at up to 120fps, enabling creators to shoot crisp talking-head videos, capture fast-moving action, and produce smooth slow-motion footage in post-production.

A dedicated AI imaging chip achieves superior low-light performance by reducing noise while preserving fine details in low light. LOFIC HDR technology supports up to 13 stops of dynamic range[1] at frame rates up to 30fps, helping retain detail in bright highlights and dark shadows.

[1]The 13-stop dynamic range is achieved under HDR recording conditions. Actual performance may vary depending on recording settings and environmental conditions.

More Professional Control Over the Final Look with OBSBOT Log

Tail Air 2 introduces OBSBOT Log, the company's proprietary 8-bit Log recording profile and the first of its kind in an OBSBOT camera. By retaining tonal information across highlights and shadows, it provides greater latitude for color grading and post-production adjustments, giving creators more control over how their footage looks.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/7f48b3f7-5e34-4fa0-a98b-8f667999c88b/obsbot-tail-air3.png

Custom 3D LUT support lets creators preview different color treatments through OBSBOT Center, Obsbot Start and Obsbot Live. They can explore a preferred look while filming or streaming, then make their final color adjustments in the edit. These previews help them decide on the visual direction before applying their final color grade in post-production.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/43a72017-38d5-4e9b-b797-ab170d4a40d5/obsbot-tail-air4.png

AI Tracking That Follows Your Story

Whether a creator is teaching, demonstrating a product or presenting alone, Tail Air 2 is designed to keep the camera focused on the action with less manual intervention. AI Tracking 2.0 recognizes people, more than 30 animal species, and over 200 object categories. Users can simply double-click a subject or draw a selection box on the control interface to tell the camera what to track.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/3d55e51f-343f-408f-a528-3c9c6cf9973b/obsbot-tail-air5.png

Beyond recognizing and following a subject, AI Tracking 2.0 also adjusts framing to suit different shooting scenarios. Single-Person Tracking maintains focus on the selected subject, even when they are briefly obscured, and reacquires them when they return. Group Tracking adjusts the camera angle and framing as people move or enter and leave the shot, maintaining a balanced composition. Face Framing leaves sufficient space in the direction a subject faces, while Auto Zoom maintains the selected full-body, medium or close-up framing as the distance changes.

Creators can further tailor how the camera responds by adjusting tracking speed, selecting a single movement axis, setting active tracking zones and customizing subject positioning within the frame. Upgraded AI Director Grids bring these controls together, allowing creators to switch between AI Tracking, Preset, and Launchpad together in one intuitive interface. Gesture Control adds another layer of hands-free operation, allowing users to control tracking, zoom and recording from up to five meters away.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/b68bfa76-b1a5-4b8c-8bfb-0757ceb7dc66/obsbot-tail-air6.png

Together, these capabilities help creators manage subject tracking, framing and camera movements within a single workflow, making it easier to produce multi-shot content without a dedicated camera operator.

More Than PTZ: Creative Movement and Native Vertical 4K

Tail Air 2 expands traditional PTZ camera movement by introducing a dedicated Roll axis, adding rotation to its Pan, Tilt, and Zoom capabilities. This PTZR architecture gives creators more ways to control camera orientation, movement, and framing.

Launchpad 2.0 makes these creative camera movements easier to execute and repeat, with eight preset camera movements and two customizable modes that allow creators to tailor camera motion to their production needs. The Roll axis also enables an Auto Leveling System that automatically corrects camera orientation to keep the horizon level, even when the camera is mounted on an uneven surface.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/9d4b9699-2119-43ad-9138-c59c8b48d734/obsbot-tail-air7.png

For vertical content, Tail Air 2 physically rotates its lens module 90 degrees to capture native vertical 4K video at up to 60fps, without cropping the sensor's full imaging area. This allows creators to switch between landscape and vertical formats while retaining the full resolution of each shot.

Together, PTZR movement and native vertical imaging give creators more control over camera movement and framing across different production formats, from livestreams and long-form videos to vertical social content.

Designed for Modern Production Workflows and Multi-Camera Setups

Built around a native IP architecture, Tail Air 2 integrates into a wide range of production environments. It supports SRT, RTSP and RTMP protocols, along with NDI®|HX3 through the NDI-enabled version or a separately purchased license, with Wi-Fi 6 and wired Ethernet connectivity for network-based video transmission. VISCA, OSC, Stream Deck integration and an Open SDK further support camera control and customized workflows.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/27161571-3335-4c8a-adc4-6da9fdcc7d8d/obsbot-tail-air8.png

For more direct production setups, Tail Air 2 offers a 3.5mm audio input, Micro HDMI output and two USB-C ports for power and data. It also supports local recording to microSD cards up to 1TB, alongside its built-in microphone and Bluetooth connectivity with OBSBOT wireless microphone Vox SE.

Tail Air 2 also features a built-in 2,630mAh battery, delivering up to 205 minutes of operation at 1080P/30fps[2], with USB PD 3.0 fast charging support.

For multi-camera productions, Tail Air 2 supports Timecode and Precision Time Protocol (PTP) synchronization. With compatible external timecode equipment, recordings from multiple cameras can be aligned more easily in post-production, while PTP helps maintain synchronized timing across networked devices.

[2]Battery life of up to 205 minutes was measured when recording at 1080P/30fps. Actual battery life may vary depending on recording resolution, frame rate, connectivity, and operating conditions.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/8317f1b5-a7ac-40a9-883b-91f504812be5/obsbot-tail-air9.png

Availability and Pricing
Tail Air 2 is offered in two versions: the Non-NDI version and the NDI version. Pre-orders opened on November 4, 2026, with a $100 discount available, and both versions are scheduled to go on sale on December 8, 2026, through the official OBSBOT online store, Amazon US, and select retailers worldwide. Pricing and availability may vary by region.

About OBSBOT
OBSBOT is a pioneer in Autonomous Imaging. Integrating core technologies across AI algorithms, motion control, and optics, OBSBOT develops intelligent agents that perceive, plan, and act to coordinate imaging hardware and production workflows—automating the capture and production process so imaging adapts to people, giving them greater freedom to express, create, and share.

Today, OBSBOT brings streamlined, professional-grade imaging to millions of users across more than 150 countries and regions in live production, video conferencing, podcasting, sports, esports, and beyond. From pioneering the world’s first auto-director AI camera and helping establish the AI PTZ webcam category to partnering with premier global tournaments, OBSBOT continues to push the boundaries of technology, pioneer next-generation imaging paradigms, and define the future of imaging.

data.title: Oil prices rise as Middle East shipping attacks counter supply surplus outlook
data.description:
* US fuel, crude stocks rise last week, EIA says

* Fed minutes, Waller comments point to more interest rate hikes

* Three oil tankers catch fire after hitting naval mines east of Hormuz - Iran media

(Changes dateline to LONDON, updates with analyst comments and prices)

By Seher Dareen

LONDON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Oil prices edged up on Thursday following losses in the prior session as worries about Middle East supplies amid attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz pushed up against expectations for a market surplus.

Brent crude futures were trading up 24 cents, or 0.26%, at $92.19 a barrel at 0953 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate futures for December were up 5 cents to $83.31. The December contract expires on Friday and the more active January contract was up 12 cents at $82.43.

While there was still uncertainty around whether oil prices would have another flare-up or break to the downside, it should be noted that Brent has not been able to stay below $90 a barrel, PVM Associates analyst John Evans said.

"There is little chance that any solution to both the Ukraine war and Iran conflict being achieved by the trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, but in the small chance something comes of it, entering into fresh length in this current environment does not seem altogether attractive," he said.

US President Donald Trump and his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, kicked off a three-way meeting, with Trump saying both he and Xi felt strongly about oil having to flow through the Strait of Hormuz.

Still, risks remained for Middle East oil supply amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

Iran's navy said three oil tankers sailing east of the Strait of Hormuz were disabled by mines, Iranian media reported on Wednesday.

On Thursday, the Iran-aligned Houthi movement fired missiles at the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh, but the Saudi Civil Defense agency said the danger had passed.

Reuters reported on Wednesday that Ukrainian drone attacks have reduced Russian oil refineries' combined crude processing volumes by 45% since late October, citing industry sources.

"Intensifying Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy infrastructure are keeping supply risks elevated for both crude oil and products, with production and exports falling," analysts at ANZ said in a note.

A larger-than-expected rise in US oil stockpiles reported on Wednesday, however, weighed on the market outlook. US crude inventories rose by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels for the week that ended on November 13, the EIA said, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for a rise of 58,000 barrels.

Brent fell 1.3% in the previous session, while WTI dropped 3.2% to its lowest point since August 26 on emerging expectations of a supply surplus.

Prices have also come under pressure from expectations of higher US interest rates that would cause lower economic growth and slower demand increases for oil. That would also strengthen the dollar, raising prices for non-US buyers paying for dollar-denominated crude in different currencies.

(Reporting by Seher Dareen in London, Colleen Howe in Beijing and Siyi Liu in Singapore; Editing by Christian Schmollinger and Thomas Derpinghaus)

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Nov 19 (Reuters) - Nasdaq futures rose nearly 2% early on Thursday after Anthropic priced its IPO above range, raising expectations for a strong market debut and lifting sentiment around battered AI stocks.

Anthropic priced its upsized offering at $83 per share, above its $70 to $78 range, raising $81 billion in the largest listing on record thatvalued the company at about $1.5 trillion. It will begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

AI-related plays in Europe, including ASML, Infineon and Siemens Energy gained about 3% each, while sentiment in Asian stocks was weaker, with Taiwan's main index down 4.4%.

The listing follows weeks of pressure on chipmakers and cloud companies, which have raised hundreds of billions of dollars to fund massive spending plans, over valuation concerns, rising AI infrastructure costs and the sudden exit of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Jensen Huang, a pillar of the industry's growth.

At 3:30 a.m. ET, Nasdaq E-minis NQc1 were up 523 points, or 1.92%, S&P 500 E-minis ESc1 were up 82.5 points, or 1.12%, and Dow E-minis YMc1 were up 359 points, or 0.71%.

The S&P 500 logged its fifth consecutive session of decline on Wednesday, with AI chip giant Nvidia ( NVDA ) ending 2.9% lower as uncertainty over co-founder Jensen Huang's recent departure overshadowed a stellar revenue forecast. Hawkish minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting added to the pressure.

Nearly all Fed officials saw a need for more rate increases if the economy performed as projected, according to the minutes, while a few warned that inflation could be stickier than anticipated and could call for tighter policy.

Traders are pricing in near-certainty of a 25-basis-point hike at the Fed's December meeting and about an 8% chance of a 50-basis-point move, according to LSEG data.

Walmart ( WMT ) reports earnings before the opening bell.

As tin demand expands beyond traditional electronics into emerging sectors such as new energy, semiconductors and AI computing, Yunnan Tin Group is pushing technological boundaries to meet higher material standards.

Yunnan Tin New Materials has developed ultra-fine solder wire with a diameter of 0.1 millimeters, while its BGA solder balls can be as small as 50 micrometers. Its solder paste portfolio covers three major series and eight product grades, catering to the trend toward increasingly compact and powerful electronic devices.

The Yunnan tin-indium laboratory focuses on green separation and high-value utilization of tin resources, comprehensive utilization of tin tailings, and the development of high-end tin-indium interconnection materials.

data.title: EMEET Advances AI Imaging for Livestreaming and Video Creation with Creator-Focused Webcam Portfolio
data.description:
HongKong, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- EMEET, a global imaging technology brand, is expanding its approach to AI-powered video creation through a portfolio of webcams designed for livestreamers, content creators, educators, and video professionals. Led by the EMEET PIXY dual-camera AI PTZ webcam, the lineup combines intelligent subject tracking, advanced image sensors, and integrated lighting solutions to address common challenges in home studios and professional video production.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/dcc251b9-7ec8-4bce-8b7f-d61709bd1824/e1.png

As livestreaming and online content creation become increasingly varied, users face practical challenges beyond video resolution. Presenters may move out of frame during demonstrations, changing lighting conditions can affect image quality, and limited workspace may make additional production equipment impractical.

EMEET's approach focuses on combining camera hardware with imaging algorithms and software tools to support more adaptable video workflows.

According to the latest IndexBox global market study, EMEET ranks second in the global webcam market, with an estimated 23% market share. Building on this position, the company continues to prioritize AI imaging innovation and creator-focused product development as key pillars of its broader imaging strategy.

EMEET PIXY Brings AI Tracking and Physical PTZ Movement to 4K Video

The EMEET PIXY serves as a central example of the company's AI imaging direction. As the world's first dual-camera AI PTZ 4K webcam, PIXY integrates AI-powered subject tracking with physical pan, tilt, and zoom movement, highlighting EMEET's continued focus on intelligent imaging innovation.

Unlike fixed-frame webcams, PIXY is designed to follow subjects as they move within a filming space, helping reduce the need for repeated manual camera adjustments.

The camera supports UHD 4K video and 1080p recording at 60 frames per second. Its 0.2s BlinkFocus autofocus is designed to respond quickly to changes in subject distance, while gesture controls allow users to manage selected camera functions without reaching for a computer.

These features are particularly relevant to online educators moving between teaching materials, creators demonstrating products, fitness instructors, and livestreamers who frequently change position during filming.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/e2a14a62-e0ea-4485-83ef-078d5d4b5b20/e2.png

EMEET is also extending the PIXY product line with PIXY Wireless, an upgraded wireless version intended to provide greater flexibility in camera placement and filming configurations.

The EMEET PIXY has earned recognition from several international design award programs, including the Red Dot Design Award, MUSE Design Award Gold, Good Design Award, and Golden Pin Design Award, highlighting its innovative design and engineering.

EMEET C960 Series Addresses Image Quality in Different Lighting Conditions

Alongside motion tracking, EMEET is developing imaging solutions focused on detail and performance across varied lighting environments.

The EMEET C960 Ultra features a 1/1.5-inch Sony image sensor, UHD 4K video support, and 0.2s BlinkFocus autofocus. Its premium aluminum alloy body is designed for home studios, video podcasts, product demonstrations, and professional video calls.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/32200c90-2cfd-4b8d-ba6b-ebb7a2aa1c32/e3.png

The camera uses Dynamic Range Control (DRC) to help manage image detail across different lighting conditions.

Building on the C960 series, the EMEET C960 UltraX introduces a larger 1/1.3-inch CMOS sensor and single-frame HDR technology. The larger sensor is designed to capture more light, while HDR processing aims to preserve detail in scenes containing both bright and dark areas.

The two models address different production requirements. The C960 Ultra provides a high-resolution option for regular creator workflows, while the UltraX adds imaging capabilities intended for more challenging conditions, including backlit rooms and dimly lit recording spaces.

EMEET identifies the broader C960 lineup as one of its best-selling webcam series.

EMEET S600L Integrates Lighting for More Convenient Video Setups

For creators working in smaller rooms or spaces without dedicated lighting equipment, the EMEET S600L combines a 4K webcam with a built-in ring light.

The camera features a 1/2-inch CMOS sensor, 0.2s BlinkFocus autofocus, and support for 4K video at 30fps or 1080p at 60fps.

Its integrated lighting system offers adjustable cool, warm, and mixed lighting modes, allowing users to adapt illumination to different recording environments.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/48578e97-7fa3-45db-ad54-99fc1ff08ce7/e4.png

By bringing lighting and video capture into one device, the S600L is designed to simplify setup for livestreaming, online teaching, video calls, and home-based content creation.

EMEET Prime Series  Brings 1-Inch Imaging to Professional Creation

The EMEET Prime series includes the flagship EMEET Prime and the EMEET Prime SE, designed for livestreamers, content creators, and professional broadcasters. The series combines advanced imaging, flexible connectivity, and intuitive software controls. Both models share a 1-inch large-format sensor, while the flagship EMEET Prime features Aurora Color, a multispectral imaging technology designed to distinguish light sources with the same color temperature but different spectral characteristics. By addressing metamerism challenges that conventional RGB imaging systems may struggle with, Aurora Color helps improve color accuracy for products such as apparel, beauty items, and jewelry, supporting more faithful product representation in livestreaming and video creation.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/e7fd0eee-51b5-434d-a1a7-b67d530dc7d7/emeet1.png

Connecting Imaging Hardware with Creator Workflows

Across these products, EMEET is pursuing a broader approach to video creation that combines intelligent camera functions with practical hardware design.

EMEET PIXY focuses on keeping moving subjects in frame, the EMEET C960 series prioritizes image detail and lighting adaptability, EMEET S600L addresses the need for a more compact production setup, and the EMEET Prime series delivers professional-grade image quality with flexible deployment.

Beyond camera hardware, EMEET is developing its software ecosystem through EMEET STUDIO, a platform that incorporates multimodal AI tools intended to support stages of content creation, including scripting, filming, editing, and publishing.

Guided by its “AI Meets Creativity” philosophy, the company aims to make imaging technology more accessible while reducing the technical demands of everyday video production.

Together, these developments reflect EMEET's strategy of moving beyond conventional webcam functions toward more flexible, intelligent, and creator-oriented imaging experiences.

About EMEET

Founded in 2016, EMEET is a global AI imaging brand that combines advanced audio-video processing with AI to deliver solutions for live streaming, content creation, and video conferencing. Its product lineup spans webcams, speakerphones, and professional headsets, with best-selling products including the EMEET PIXY series, C960 Ultra, and S600L, among others.

EMEET holds more than 200 core patents worldwide and has earned recognition from major international design awards, including iF, Red Dot, the Good Design Award (G Mark), and IDEA. Its webcams have ranked among the top in Amazon Best Sellers across major marketplaces, including No. 1 positions in the webcam category. According to IndexBox, EMEET ranks as the No. 2 webcam brand with a 23% market share.

data.title: FOREX-Dollar eases after seven-session rally, rates and equities in focus
data.description:
* Dollar edges down but still near highest since April 2, 2025

* Yen falls against dollar, euro after safe-haven rally

* Hawkish Fed signals keep further rate hikes on investors' radar

(Recasts with fresh comments, adds background)

By Stefano Rebaudo

Nov 19 (Reuters) - The US dollar index edged down on Thursday after a seven-session winning streak but remained underpinned by hawkish remarks from a Federal Reserve official that reinforced the case for further rate hikes.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller called for a more aggressive response to inflation, while minutes of the central bank's October 27 to 28 meeting showed policymakers increasingly concerned that additional tightening might be needed.

The dollar rally started on November 10 when hotter-than-expected US inflation data bolstered expectations that the Fed would raise borrowing costs next month.

The dollar index this week reached its highest level since April 2, 2025, when US President Donald Trump revealed a sweeping tariff package, triggering a selloff in US assets.

It was last down 0.05% at 103.73, after reaching 103.97.

Barclays analysts said fiscal stimulus and strong AI-related capital spending point to a resilient US economy, a wider output gap and higher-for-longer interest rates, all supportive of dollar strength.

The dollar's gains have come despite a selloff in technology shares.

"First, the market has also repriced a more hawkish Fed given recent commentary pushing the interest rate differential wider, but the dollar seems to be overshooting this move," said George Saravelos, global head of forex strategy at Deutsche Bank, explaining the recent rise.

"Second, and more intriguingly, foreigners have been very aggressive buyers of US equities even as the stock market has tumbled," he added.

A Deutsche Bank tracker following more than 100 foreign-domiciled exchange-traded funds showed large dip-buying of US stocks by foreigners over the last two weeks, the biggest buying spree so far this year.

Such a move reinforces the view that the dollar has been supported by investor flows into US equities.

Shares in Nvidia ( NVDA ) fell overnight even after the chip bellwether beat revenue and guidance forecasts, amid uncertainty caused by co-founder Jensen Huang's sudden departure as CEO last week following his admission of extramarital affairs.

SAFE-HAVEN FLOWS BOOST THE YEN

The dollar was up 0.25% to 159.75 yen, snapping a four-day losing streak.

Analysts said that a further selloff in AI-linked assets could support the yen through safe-haven buying and repatriation flows, with the impact likely to be more pronounced against other currencies than against the dollar.

According to Barclays estimates, a 10% decline in the S&P 500 from its peak could push dollar/yen towards 155, while a 20% decline could pressure it towards 152.

The euro was up 0.34% versus the Japanese currency at 175.43, after falling about 1.5% since late last week.

The Aussie dropped as low as $0.6662 for the first time since January. Australia's employment fell for a second straight month in October and the jobless rate climbed to a five-year high, bolstering the view that rates have likely peaked.

Following the data, UBS economist George Tharenou brought forward his forecast for the first Reserve Bank of Australia rate cut to August next year from November, and extended the easing cycle to three cuts from two, citing elevated inflation and a deterioration in the labour and housing markets.

  • The pipeline system transport chemicals and industrial feedstocks (e.g. ammonia), providing logistics services to industrial facilities in the Houston Ship Channel area

  • The transaction supports Exolum’s growth strategy in the United States, building on its existing capabilities and resources in Houston

HOUSTON, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Exolum has completed the acquisition of a pipeline system from Boardwalk serving industrial customers in the Houston Ship Channel area.

The acquired infrastructure provides dedicated transportation services to industrial facilities in the Houston Ship Channel area. The acquisition expands Exolum’s capabilities in the United States by adding pipeline transportation to its existing storage and logistics operations in Houston.

The acquisition builds on Exolum’s established presence in Houston and will enable the new operations to benefit from the company’s existing capabilities, resources and local experience. By combining ammonia storage and logistics with pipeline transportation, Exolum will offer a broader range of integrated logistics solutions while assuming direct responsibility for pipeline operations, integrity and regulatory compliance in the United States.

Image: Exolum acquires pipeline system

“This acquisition represents an important step in the development of Exolum’s business in the United States. It allows us to build on our existing capabilities in Houston, bring our international pipeline experience to the U.S. market and broaden the logistics services we provide to industrial customers. We remain committed to growing our presence in the country in a disciplined and sustainable way,” said Javier Goñi, CEO of Exolum.

The newly acquired pipelines will be operated in line with Exolum’s rigorous safety, integrity and operational standards, supporting the reliable and continuous supply of raw materials to industrial facilities in the Houston Ship Channel area. This type of infrastructure plays an important role in strengthening industrial supply chains and supporting essential manufacturing processes.

About Exolum

Exolum is Europe’s leading logistics company for liquid products and one of the largest in the world. Its core business is sustainable, efficient transport and storage of a wide range of bulk liquid products, particularly refined and chemical products and biofuels. It also operates in new sectors, such as eco-fuels, the circular economy and the development of new energy vectors. The company operates in ten countries (Spain, Portugal, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Germany, France, the Netherlands, United States of America, Panama, and Peru) with a pipeline network of over 6,000 kilometers, 68 storage terminals and 50 airport facilities, and a total storage capacity of more than 11 million cubic meters. For more information, please visit www.exolum.com.
 
About Boardwalk Pipelines, LP
‍
Boardwalk Pipelines, LP (“Boardwalk”) delivers reliable energy by connecting natural gas supply with the markets and communities that depend on it. Through an integrated network of interstate and intrastate pipelines and underground storage assets, Boardwalk supports energy reliability, market connectivity and long-term value creation across the United States, including the Gulf Coast, Midwest and Southeast. Boardwalk is committed to operating safely, reliably and responsibly while evolving its capabilities to better serve customers in a dynamic and increasingly complex energy market. Learn more at bwpipelines.com.

data.title: Anthropic raises record $81 billion in IPO at $1.5 trillion valuation
data.description:
Nov 18 (Reuters) - Anthropic has raised $81.3 billion in the largest stock-market debut on record after upsizing its offering, valuing the Claude chatbot maker at $1.5 trillion in a deal that defies concerns about the AI trade and tech fundraising prospects.

The first major frontier AI model developer to go public, Anthropic on Wednesday priced its shares at $83 apiece, above its initial range of $70 to $78, in a sign of strong demand for the shares from investors.

Reuters was first to report earlier on Wednesday that the company increased the number of shares it was selling by about 19% to 980 million shares. The upsized IPO eclipsed the previous record-setting debut of Elon Musk's SpaceX in June.

The total deal size is $107.3 billion, including another $26 billion Anthropic is raising through a private placement of shares at the IPO price, the filings showed.

Anthropic comes to the public market even as the backdrop for AI stocks has turned challenging.

In recent weeks chipmakers and cloud companies, which have raised hundreds of billions of dollars to fund their massive spending plans, have come under pressure due to valuation concerns, mounting AI infrastructure costs and the sudden exit of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Jensen Huang, a pillar of the industry's growth.

At the same time, Anthropic has faced questions about its outlook and ability to sustain rapid growth as competition in the industry intensifies.

Armina Rosenberg, portfolio manager and co-founder of Minotaur Capital, which is awaiting an Anthropic share allocation, said the company's IPO was a useful gauge of investor appetite for AI.

"But one listing won't settle the debate. There's a genuine wall of worry right now, and it'll take a few things to climb it. Once Anthropic reports publicly, it becomes one of the clearest tests of whether the economics of AI are holding up," she said.

On a fully diluted basis, the IPO now values the company at about $1.5 trillion, including securities such as stock options and restricted stock. On a non-diluted basis, the valuation stands at about $1.1 trillion.

US stock futures were up after Anthropic's IPO details were made public, while Asian tech stocks remained under pressure amid broader concerns about the AI trade. Anthropic is set to start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT.

A strong debut could give confidence to other companies waiting to tap public markets. Anthropic's closest rival, OpenAI, is expected to pursue a listing as early as next year.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley ( MS ) are the lead underwriters for Anthropic's offering, which has a 22-bank underwriting syndicate. The two banks also served as lead underwriters for SpaceX's IPO earlier this year. 

SPENDING COMMITMENTS EXPOSE RISKS

Anthropic's growth has been driven by surging demand for its Claude models, particularly Claude Code, its coding agent that has gained popularity among software developers. Its annualized revenue run rate reached $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30, according to its IPO filing.

The Claude maker said it had 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue on a trailing 12-month basis as of September 30, compared with more than 1,500 at the end of last year, underscoring its growing business foothold.

But sustaining that growth is becoming expensive. Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, nearly four times the amount spent a year earlier.

It also incurred an additional $5 billion in computing costs in the third quarter, reducing the revenue generated per dollar of computing capacity.

Revenue rose 47% in the third quarter to $16.96 billion from the second quarter. The company reported an operating loss of $567 million, compared with operating income of $974 million in the previous quarter.

The net loss narrowed to $23.3 billion from $66.3 billion a quarter earlier, including non-operating ​items related to bonds convertible into its shares. 

Anthropic has committed to nearly $900 billion in computing spending with infrastructure partners, including Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet's Google, to train and operate AI models.

It warned that its computing providers and infrastructure partners depend on third-party financing and credit support to acquire chips and build capacity. 

"If such financing or support becomes unavailable or more costly, contracted capacity may be delayed, repriced, reduced, or not delivered," Anthropic said in an IPO filing. 

COMPETITION AND SAFETY CHALLENGES

Anthropic faces questions over how it will balance its commercial ambitions with its emphasis on AI safety.

CEO Dario Amodei has called for the industry to slow the pace of developing and releasing increasingly powerful models, warning that advances in AI could outstrip society's ability to manage the risks.

"Our development of highly advanced models, platforms, and applications and expansion of use cases could further increase the risk that our models cause harm," Anthropic said in the filing.

At the same time, competition is intensifying against Anthropic to be the leading provider of AI tools for businesses.

OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, its latest flagship AI model, accounted for about 13% of enterprise AI spending tracked by corporate expense platform Ramp, compared with about 8% for Anthropic's Claude Fable, according to data cited by Reuters in September.

The competitive threat extends beyond the handful of companies developing the most powerful commercial models. A recent Capgemini study found that 59% of executives at large companies plan to increase their use of open-weight models over the next year as AI costs exceed budgets.

Meta Platforms, one of Anthropic's largest customers, has been looking to reduce its use of the startup's models as it develops more AI capabilities internally, Reuters previously reported.

"Our thesis is that the vast amount of value will accrue to whoever is at the frontier," said Peter Singlehurst, head of private companies at Baillie Gifford, which invested roughly $1.5 billion in Anthropic before its IPO.

"Our bet is that Anthropic has the ingredients - that doesn't guarantee, but means that they arguably have the highest probability of remaining at the frontier."

(Reporting by Echo Wang in New York; additional reporting by Ankur Banerjee in Singapore; Editing by David Gaffen, Christian Plumb, Matthew Lewis and Sonali Paul)

data.title: OVHcloud launches AI cloud products hosted in Europe
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - OVHcloud said on Thursday it had launched 55 cloud-computing and AI products that run on infrastructure hosted in Europe, including access to Nvidia's ( NVDA ) latest AI chips and a workplace application combining email, documents and videoconferencing with AI assistants.

The French cloud provider said its data centres could take up to 60,000 of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Blackwell chips, a capacity it said matched the largest global platforms.

OVHcloud also announced partnerships with cloud-computing company Shadow, Qwant and EUSP, a joint venture between Qwant and Ecosia that develops a European search index.

Qwant and OVHcloud said that AI-generated summaries appearing in the search engine's results would be powered by OVHcloud's Olala model and hosted in European data centres.

The move comes as European governments and companies increasingly scrutinise where AI services are operated and how their data is handled, creating opportunities for regional providers seeking to compete with US cloud and AI firms.

(Reporting by Leo Marchandon, writing by Emanuele Berro, editing by Milla Nissi-Prussak)

data.title: Osaka Gas to expand US, India business despite global geopolitical risks
data.description:
TOKYO, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Japanese gas utility Osaka Gas ( OSGSF ) will continue expanding its businesses in the US and India despite rising global geopolitical risks, President Masataka Fujiwara said on Thursday.

* Osaka Gas ( OSGSF ) produces and sells US shale gas to domestic customers, and is expanding sales of domestically produced natural gas and renewable energy development in India

* The company is not concerned about securing liquefied natural gas supplies for the peak winter demand season as it has no contracts requiring shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and has secured most supplies under long-term contracts, Executive Officer Sunao Okamoto said

* However, lower-than-usual European gas inventories could lead to competition between Europe and Asia for spot LNG after the winter, potentially pushing up prices, Okamoto said

* Osaka Gas ( OSGSF ) decided to exit the Greater Sunrise gas project, whose gas fields lie between East Timor and Australia, after participating since 2000, as development had made little progress and it was time to move on as part of a portfolio reshuffle, Okamoto said

* In September, Osaka Gas ( OSGSF ) bought a 5% stake in Australia's Browse gas project. Okamoto said the company expects the project to eventually move forward and values Australia as a Japanese ally with no major shipping chokepoints. The project would also allow Osaka Gas ( OSGSF ) to secure LNG on a free-on-board basis from its own equity production

* Osaka Gas ( OSGSF ) has long-term LNG contracts with Australia, the US, Papua New Guinea and Russia, after contracts with Malaysia, Brunei and Oman expired in recent years. Its LNG transaction volume reached 12.4 million metric tons in the financial year that ended March 2026, with 20% coming from its equity investments in upstream gas projects

(Reporting by Yuka Obayashi. Editing by Mark Potter)

data.title: 'GTA VI' to supercharge Sony - but not so much in Japan
data.description:
* About three-quarters of 17 million GTA VI units sold on PlayStation - estimate

* Sony to see large royalties benefit - analyst

* Japan's gaming device market is dominated by Nintendo ( NTDOF )

* Marketing in Japan unprecedented for Western-made game- expert

By Sam Nussey, Anton Bridge and Kentaro Okasaka

TOKYO, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The global launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI" on Thursday is expected to provide a major boost to PlayStation maker Sony,though in its home market of Japan, the franchise remains a niche pursuit.

The long-awaited open-world crime action game from Take-Two Interactive's Rockstar Games is rolling out across the world and has been met with rave reviews and fans taking time off work to play.

About three-quarters of the 17 million "GTA VI" units sold are on PlayStation, according to estimates from Sensor Tower, outselling Xbox maker Microsoft ( MSFT ).

Shares in Sony, whose PlayStation 5 console is in its seventh year on the market, were up almost 3% in Tokyo compared with flat trading in the benchmark index.

Analysts think the global enthusiasm is unlikely to reach a fever pitch in Japan, where Switch 2 maker Nintendo ( NTDOF ) dominates the gaming device market and consumers prefer anime-style titles to realistic, violent Western games.

"The current trends in Japan don't really fit this kind of game," said Toyo Securities analyst Hideki Yasuda.

Given worldwide demand, "there's absolutely no need for this game to sell in Japan," he said.

Earlier this year Sony scored a major global success with movie "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" but in Japan faced competition from breakout hit "Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of Mermaid Island."

"A few of my friends bought 'GTA VI' at midnight but I'm in no hurry to as it's only on PS5 and Xbox and you can't play multiplayer online yet," said Sorataka Goto, 33, who was shopping in Tokyo's Akihabara electronics district.

"If and when it's on PC and you can play online I'll consider buying it," said Goto, who bought the remake of "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time".

Nintendo ( NTDOF ) has sold more than five million copies of the Switch 2 title, which was originally on the Nintendo ( NTDOF ) 64, in the first four days since its launch earlier this month.

"I had the original as a child and so was excited to try this version," he said.

JAPAN NOT IMMUNE TO 'GTA VI' HYPE

Gamers in Japan may struggle to fully understand the satirical elements of "GTA VI", the references to the Florida lifestyle and Western memes, said Serkan Toto, founder of game industry consultancy Kantan Games.

Still, the worldwide hype for "GTA VI" is spilling over to Japan and marketing in the country is unprecedented for a Western-made game, he said.

In Akihabara, a large poster featuring the lead characters, Lucia Caminos ​and Jason Duval, was plastered on the side of a building.

"'GTA VI' will not become a mega blockbuster in Japan but it will do very, very well," Toto said.

Analysts expect the release of "GTA VI" to soften the decline of PS5 hardware sales this year and support growth in software sales.

Sony sold 2.6 million PS5 units during the July to September quarter, which analysts see as reflecting demand ahead of "GTA VI", down from 4 million a year earlier.

"We've modeled PlayStation profits materially ahead of the Street in the next couple of quarters, on account of the 'GTA VI' launch," Bernstein analyst David Dai wrote in a note.

The release is bolstering Sony's ( SONY ) games slate after it delayed the launch of "God of War Laufey" by three months to May 2027.

Sony is grappling with procurement challenges as the cost of memory chips has risen sharply due to the AI boom.

"I don't get the sense that Sony has much desire to aggressively sell hardware... the benefits Sony gets from royalties will be enormous," said Toyo Securities' Yasuda.

(Reporting by Sam Nussey and Kentaro Okasaka; Editing by Kate Mayberry)

data.description:
* Taiwan closes 4.4% lower
    * MSCI EM Asia hits lowest since April
    * Rupiah weakens toward record low

    (Updates for afternoon trade)
    By Rajasik Mukherjee
       Nov 19 (Reuters) - Asian stocks sank to their lowest
level in more than seven months on Thursday, dragged by a nearly
5% drop in Taiwanese shares, while regional currencies traded
cautiously ahead of a high-stakes meeting between the leaders of
the United States, China and Russia.
    The MSCI emerging Asia equities index
declined as much as 2.6% to its lowest since early April.
    Stocks in Taiwan fell as much as 4.8% to their
lowest level in nearly two weeks, before closing 4.4% lower.
    The benchmark has lost more than 10% this week, prompting
Taiwan's financial regulator to announce fresh curbs on short
selling, citing weak investor confidence and heightened market
volatility amid an uncertain global political and economic
backdrop.
    Home to TSMC, the world's largest contract
chipmaker and a key supplier to Nvidia ( NVDA ), Taiwan's market
has been one of the biggest beneficiaries of the artificial
intelligence boom, drawing global investors betting on sustained
demand for advanced semiconductors.
    "Tighter US regulatory and chip export policies are raising
concerns about disruption to the regional semiconductor and AI
supply chains," said Lukman Leong, chief analyst at Doo
Financial Futures.
    "Investors have also reportedly been reducing positions in
Asian semiconductor stocks to raise cash ahead of Anthropic's
massive IPO."
    South Korea's KOSPI, home to major technology and
chip stocks, fell as much as 2.1% on the day, before ending the
day 1.4% in the green.
    Thai stocks fell as much as 1.2% to their lowest
since April-end, while those in Malaysia fell 0.2% and
the Philippines shed 0.8%. Indonesian stocks fell
0.5%, set for a fourth consecutive session of decline.
    Regional currencies largely treaded water as traders awaited
potential trade and geopolitical signals from a historic meeting
between US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping
and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
    The Indonesian rupiah was the worst performer in the
region, weakening as much as 0.3% to 18,272, a whisker away from
a record low logged earlier this week.
     The depreciation comes a day after Bank Indonesia
unexpectedly raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 6%,
the highest since January 2025.
    "Rupiah's renewed weakness reflects persistent external and
domestic pressures," Leong added.
    "Concerns over fiscal health, policy consistency, governance
and foreign capital outflows are adding further pressure... rate
hike may provide some support, but higher interest rates alone
cannot reverse the trend."
    The Thai baht touched its weakest level since April
2025 before trimming losses to trade flat by 0706 GMT.
    Elsewhere in the region, the Singapore dollar, the
Philippine peso, and the Malaysian ringgit were

data.title: TIMELINE-Germany and UniCredit reach broad agreement in Commerzbank takeover battle
data.description:
(Updates timeline last published on August 26)

By Tom Sims and Valentina Za

FRANKFURT, Nov 19 (Reuters) - UniCredit ​and Germany have reached agreement on the big sticking points in the Italian bank's takeover of Commerzbank, a major ‌development in the two-year battle for control of the German lender.

Like some other banks, Commerzbank has had a rocky history with big mergers and acquisitions over the years, including a long pursuit by UniCredit.

These are some of the key moments:

1870 to 1970s

Founded in Hamburg and later moved to Berlin. Relocated to Frankfurt in 1970 as one of Germany's leading banks, focusing on retail and corporate customers.

1970s

Expands to New York, London and other European capitals.

2008

Agrees to buy Dresdner Bank, one of Germany's biggest banks, from insurer Allianz in a $14.5 billion deal.

Commerzbank is the first commercial bank to turn to the German government for capital during the global financial crisis.

2009

With the bailout, Germany takes a 25% plus one share stake in Commerzbank in return for an extra €10 billion ($11.4 billion) capital injection.

2016

Commerzbank embarks on a multi-year restructuring.

2017

US investor Cerberus builds a stake controlling 5% of Commerzbank voting rights. UniCredit tells Berlin it is interested in eventually merging with Commerzbank to create one of Europe's biggest banks.

2018

Commerzbank drops out of the blue-chip DAX index.

2019

Cerberus says it is open to a merger between Deutsche Bank and Commerzbank. The two institutions hold talks, but call them off weeks later.

UniCredit hires investment bankers to advise it on a potential bid for Commerzbank, whose supervisory board approves cutting thousands of jobs and closing a fifth of its branches.

2020

In a U-turn, Commerzbank says it would not sell Polish subsidiary mBank, citing poor market conditions.

Commerzbank chairman and CEO step down, bowing to Cerberus demands.

2021

New CEO Manfred Knof wants to cut 10,000 jobs and close hundreds of branches as part of a revamp. Knof says Commerzbank is working to remain independent.

2022-2023

UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel approaches Knof about a deal in early 2022, before the Ukraine war, Reuters reports. Meanwhile, Commerzbank returns to profit and rejoins the DAX.

2024

September 11 - UniCredit approaches Commerzbank about exploring a merger, according to a person with knowledge of the matter, after the Italian bank buys a 9% stake. Commerzbank's management discusses how to keep it independent.

September 13 - German government officials and UniCredit bankers hold talks, Reuters reports.

September 16 - Knof snubs UniCredit's overtures, saying he has his own plans and hopes his bank can remain independent.

September 20 - Germany says it would not sell any more shares in Commerzbank for now.

September 23 - German Chancellor Olaf Scholz calls UniCredit's move to acquire a possible 21% stake "an unfriendly attack".

September 24 - Commerzbank picks its finance chief Bettina Orlopp as new CEO.

October 1 - Orlopp, on her first day as CEO, tells staff she wants Commerzbank to remain independent.

December 18 - UniCredit announces an increase in its stake through derivatives to around 28%.

2025

January 31 - Commerzbank posts a 20% increase in net profit in 2024 in an earnings report published nearly two weeks ahead of schedule.

February 13 - Commerzbank plans to axe 3,900 mostly local jobs to help it deliver more ambitious profit targets.

March 14 - Commerzbank takes note of ECB approval of UniCredit's stake rise but remains focused on its strategy.

2026

March 16 - UniCredit launches unsolicited bid to raise its stake above 30%. Commerzbank, the German government and a key union voice reservations.

April 7 - Short-lived talks between the banks fall apart.

May 5 - UniCredit formally launches its bid.

May 8 - Commerzbank updates its strategy with earnings.

May 18 - Commerzbank formally rejects UniCredit's offer.

June 4 - Commerzbank raises concerns with the German regulator about UniCredit's disclosures on its stake buildup.

June 16 - Germany, which holds Commerzbank shares, officially rejects ‌UniCredit's offer.

July 8 - UniCredit announces it has secured 47.6% of Commerzbank shares.

August 6 - Orlopp says a tie-up with UniCredit could create value for both sides, in a significant shift of tone.

August 26 - German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil and Orcel plan to meet.

September 14 - Klingbeil sets out demands to UniCredit.

September 15 - Orcel does not want Orlopp to remain as Commerzbank CEO, Reuters reports.

October 16 - UniCredit wins European Central Bank support.

November 5 - Commerzbank says it is "convinced" a deal could create value.

November 19 - Berlin and UniCredit broadly agree to deal.

($1 = €0.8752)

(Reporting by Tom Sims, John O'Donnell and Valentina Za; Editing by Alexander Smith, Tomasz Janowski, Edwina Gibbs and Joe Bavier)

data.title: Riyadh skyscraper housing Saudi wealth fund damaged in Houthi strike, sources say
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - A Houthi missile attack damaged a skyscraper in Riyadh housing the offices of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund PIF on Thursday, three people familiar with the matter said, in the Iran-allied group's latest blow to the kingdom in their escalating war.

The attack on King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD), which includes Riyadh's tallest building, is the second this month, after a strike by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on November 8 damaged Saudi oil giant Aramco's building.

All entrances to the district were closed and people were being evacuated, while ambulances and fire trucks were present, a Reuters witness said.

PIF said it will revert back to a Reuters request for comment

The Saudi-led coalition fighting the powerful militia said earlier that it had dealt with a missile launched by the Houthis towards Riyadh, adding that an initial assessment showed debris had fallen and material damage had been reported, but added that the extent of the damage was still being determined.

The escalation in fighting between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest crude exporter, has become another front in the wider US-Israeli war on Iran, which has seen an uptick in hostilities in recent days despite diplomatic efforts to end the nine-month-old conflict.

The Houthis have yet to claim the attack.

Saudi aircraft carried out airstrikes on the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital Sanaa early on Thursday, the Houthi-run Saba news agency reported shortly afterwards without providing further details.

(Reporting by Enas Alashray and Timour Azhari; Editing by Jacqueline Wong, Thomas Derpinghaus, Edwina Gibbs, Alexandra Hudson)

data.title: Taiwan to enact new short-selling curbs in response to market drop
data.description:
TAIPEI, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Taiwan's financial regulator said on Thursday it will enact new short-selling curbs after the benchmark index ended down 4.4%, extending falls as investors were unnerved by the future of AI after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO.

Taiwan, a major producer of the advanced chips driving the AI revolution, has already put into operation a $15 billion stock stabilisation fund as well as previously announced short-selling curbs.

The Financial Supervisory Commission said in a statement that under the new restrictions, when a stock closes down 3.5% or more on a given day, investors may not sell it short through margin short selling or borrowed securities on the next trading day.

The regulator noted sharp swings in share prices but said stock fundamentals remain fairly solid, listed companies have posted record revenue, and the capital market is resilient.

Investor confidence is weak, it said.

A senior regulatory official told Reuters that the latest round of short-selling restrictions is mainly aimed at "cracking down on bearish forces in the Taiwan stock market and preventing short sellers' influence from expanding".

The official spoke on condition of anonymity as they were not authorised to speak to the media.

The regulator also said it will continue to monitor changes in the international financial situation and conditions in the domestic capital market, and adjust stabilisation measures as appropriate.

(Reporting by Ben Blanchard and Emily Chan; Editing by Christopher Cushing and Jacqueline Wong)

data.title: Fed policymakers concerned about financial system risks, minutes show
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Financial stability risks tied to aggressive artificial intelligence investment and elevated asset prices are on the US central bank's radar, the minutes from the Federal Reserve's policy meeting last month showed on Wednesday.

The concern was raised as part of a broad review of financial risks by Fed policymakers and central bank staff at the October 27-28 policy meeting. That gathering saw officials hold interest rates steady despite ongoing worries about high and persistent levels of inflation. However, "almost all" policymakers agreed that further hikes would be needed if the economy evolved as they expected, the minutes showed. 

"The staff judged that current vulnerabilities could amplify shocks somewhat more than usual, with elevated asset valuations and leverage at hedge funds representing the most salient vulnerabilities, while strong bank and household balance sheets provided an important buffer against more severe outcomes," the minutes said.

Policymakers expressed concern that huge levels of investment in AI technology could lead to trouble and create broader problems for both the financial system and economy.

"Almost all participants commented on risks associated with a scenario in which the returns on AI investment turned out to be disappointing to investors," the minutes said. "Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures," while "a few" of the unnamed Fed officials were concerned that AI exposure was being concentrated in a "small number" of companies.

Fed officials also cast an anxious eye toward hedge funds.

"Most participants highlighted hedge fund leverage or limited dealer intermediation capacity as potential channels of amplification during periods of market stress," the minutes said.

Fed staff described the financial system as "resilient," with banks having ample access to cash, according to the minutes. But some policymakers worried that "banking system vulnerabilities could emerge rapidly even after seemingly reassuring initial assessments."

Some were also worried the Fed's data on the banking system may miss the full range of exposure some financial firms have.

BUILDING RESILIENCE

Financial markets have been under stress in recent weeks amid questions about the future of AI and how the buildout of the technology has increasingly come to rely on debt. Past periods of financial trouble have been frequently associated with excessive borrowing, and some of those crises have driven the Fed to intervene to stabilize markets.

The latest minutes also showed Fed officials weighing how they can respond to future troubles.

"A few" policymakers mulled boosting banks' capital levels while some also said it is important to better prepare banks to use the Fed's emergency lending discount window facility, which is something officials have been working on for some time.

In addition, "a few" policymakers considered a novel strategy in which the Fed would set up a dedicated method of asset-buying that would explicitly target financial stability concerns.

The Fed is weighing the future of how it uses its balance sheet as a policy tool. Fed holdings have swollen massively over the last two decades due to huge bond purchases during the 2008 global financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic.

The pandemic experience has loomed particularly large because bond-buying that began in March 2020 started out as a stabilization tool that morphed into outright stimulus.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack is among those who would like to see a more clearly defined system for buying bonds that would also entail a strategy to sell them when a crisis has passed. Hammack said earlier this week that any program "should also be temporary, and holdings should be sold in a timely way once market financial stability is restored." 

The minutes noted that "several" policymakers cautioned that monetary policy is not the right tool to deal with market trouble. But the large role now played by AI and technology investment in driving economic growth might complicate that view if large-scale problems emerged.

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby; Editing by Paul Simao)

data.title: ROI-The 'AI dollar' has arrived. Its direction hasn't: Mike Dolan
data.description:
(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters.)

By Mike Dolan

LONDON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - AI is increasingly shaping the fortunes of the US dollar, or at least the investment race surrounding it. The only problem is currency experts can't agree whether that's for better or worse.

Few doubt that seemingly Teflon US economic growth over the past two years has been enormously flattered by the impact of the burgeoning AI boom.

That reflects the trillion-dollar explosion in investment in AI data centers, chips and computing equipment, as well as the more nebulous "wealth effects" from accompanying stock price gains.

Estimates vary, but many analysts say AI is directly or indirectly responsible for at least a third of US gross domestic product (GDP) expansion this year.

That alone seems straightforward, but the extent to which the dollar's value is AI-linked is more nuanced.

Some focus on the US AI lead over other economies as a dollar driver, but others view an "AI dollar" through a balance-of-payments lens and the prism of cross-border capital flows.

No one doubts AI's importance to currency markets. How it plays out is another matter.

AI AND THE FED

At its most basic, the lift to US growth, inflation and interest rate expectations from the AI boom is clearly dollar positive - as long as the US retains its edge and the lion's share of the investment being ploughed into it.

While that may change as the early US investment surge slows, we're not there yet in most people's eyes. The dollar is clearly reflecting expectations that the Federal Reserve may hike rates aggressively to cool an AI-fueled boom and rein in inflation, with investors convinced the economy can take it while other central banks hesitate.

Since the Iran war began at the end of February, the US economy has brushed aside the related fuel-price shock with ease, and the AI story seems largely responsible.

As a measure of how those downbeat expectations proved wide of the mark, US economic surprise indexes compiled by Citi have hit their most positive level in three years this month, contrasting starkly with euro zone equivalents, which have turned negative again for the first time in four months.

Little surprise, then, that euro/dollar has fallen below $1.10 this week for the first time since March last year, while the broader dollar index has hit its best level in more than 19 months.

AI CUTS FX OUTLOOK BOTH WAYS

But wait. This dollar surge is happening just as Big Tech investors get the jitters over AI valuations and on fear of a capital expenditure slowdown after Democratic victories in the midterm elections prompt calls for at least some data-center pushback.

The scale of the shakeout in AI-linked stocks has been withering for six weeks, seeing almost 30% wiped off the US Philadelphia Semiconductor Index since early October.

So, why hasn't the fabled "AI dollar" gone with it?

Is the greenback simply lagging, or staying laser-focused on pumped-up Fed rate-rise expectations? Or maybe it's getting a safety bid from worries about equity-market turbulence?

Barclays FX strategists this week reckoned their bullish "AI dollar" view remains very much intact for next year.

Their take hinges on the fact the dollar is mainly tracking AI capex numbers that have been driving GDP outperformance, forcing the Fed to rethink the level of slack left in the economy and where neutral interest rates lie.

And so despite the shakeout in AI stock prices, there's still been no change to estimates of hyperscaler investment spending through next year - not even since the midterms.

As a result, the Barclays team thinks the dollar will continue to gorge on that rather than the volatile equity market per se.

But there are as many questions in that as there are answers.

A severe tech-stock correction or even rout could well eat into investment plans quite quickly and douse any "wealth effect" from the AI-fueled stock rally of the past 18 months.

A downshift in AI build-out then starts to shave GDP bets, easing upward pressure on Fed rates and ultimately weighing on the buck.

How likely is that?

Bank of America's November survey of global fund managers offers some insight. The poll showed asset managers this month cut tech allocations by the most in 20 years, with a record net near 40% of respondents saying companies are "over-investing."

Perhaps most telling, more than half of the funds expect at least one hyperscaler to cut capex in the next six months.

So AI capex can still be your lodestar, but it may not mean the "AI dollar" is the slam dunk for 2027 that markets have recently rushed to price.

'CHIPDOLLARS'

However, there's another way to view the nexus between AI and the dollar.

Deutsche Bank introduces its idea of "chipdollars," akin to the petrodollars of old. World chip trade now exceeds oil and gas for the first time in history, it says, suggesting a less favorable outlook for the dollar.

The gist of Deutsche's view is that most US-designed chips are made outside the US, mainly in Asia.

As chip demand has soared and prices have risen, huge surpluses have built up in these countries. Much of that cash has been recycled into US capital markets, mostly equities rather than Treasury debt as in the past.

Estimating foreign flows into US equities this year at more than $1 trillion, the German bank said this funding of US deficits is supporting the dollar and financing firms driving the AI build, then flowing back into chips in another loop of cross-border "circularity."

However, a big problem is that equities are three times more volatile than Treasuries, and tech stocks up to 10 times more so.

"Growing dollar dependence on inherently riskier capital should spill into higher US dollar volatility over time," Deutsche strategist Mallika Sachdeva wrote.

There's no doubt the "AI dollar" is now a thing. It's just that it could go either way next year - not unlike its analog predecessor.

(The opinions expressed here are those of Mike Dolan, a columnist for Reuters.)
